documents.t: By the end of this session, you will be able to: Set up the Private Node development environment and understand the TypeScript entity file structure. Understand the entity lifecycle and all hook methods: onAfterCreate, OnValidate, onDelete. Write and test server-side default value logic: auto-set s_status = OPEN and assigned_to = current user on complaint creation. Implement property-level Getter and Setter overrides to compute derived fields (actual_tat, full customer display). Write business rule validations in OnValidate: mandatory field checks, date constraints, role-based restriction. Implement query-level beforeQ / afterQ callbacks: enforce row-level, role-based visibility before a query runs, and reshape/compute values across the result set after it returns. Apply the landing page concept: prepare the p_complaints page to function as the application's primary home screen post-login. 📘 What This Session Builds On Sessions 1–4 built the data model, page structure, VH pickers, and queries — all through the low-code tools (Data Studio, Page Builder). Session 5 crosses the threshold into code: you will write TypeScript in the entity .ts file, running server-side in the Klobase Node.js runtime. The entity file is the ONLY place business logic belongs. Never write business rules in the controller file. Session 5 follows the core platform principle: Business logic → Entity file. UI orchestration → Controller file. Reference: PROC-23582 (Validation Logic to Be Maintained in Entity Callback onValidate Methods instead of Controller files).

documents.t: Every control on a Klobase screen reads and writes data through the Transaction Model ($M). The model is a JSON model object. All bindings use the prefix $M to reference it. Without a binding, a control shows a static value or nothing at all — it is disconnected from the live data.
documents.s: Part A — Data Bindings In Depth
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part A — Data Bindings In Depth

documents.t: The Transaction Model is organized as a tree. Each TransNode in the Page Data Model corresponds to a branch in the $M tree. The full path to any property follows this pattern: {$M>/transNodeRelationId/propertyId} For a list TransNode with relationId = list, the first row's complaint_desc is: {$M>/list/0/complaint_desc} For the detail TransNode with relationId = detail: {$M>/detail/complaint_desc} The leading / after > is mandatory. Omitting it causes a silent bind failure.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part A — Data Bindings In Depth

documents.t: Mode When to Use Syntax / Where to Set Example Value Static, hardcoded value — no model connection. Control always shows this literal text regardless of data. Properties tab → Value field text = 'Complaint ID' — always shows that label. Path Bind to exactly ONE model property. Two-way binding by default: changes in UI write back to model. Properties tab → DSRC field {$M>/detail/complaint_desc} — shows and edits the complaint description. Parts Combine MULTIPLE paths into one display value via a formatter function. Always one-way (read only). Properties tab → dsrc field (add each path as a part) + Formatter Function field Parts: {$M>/detail/first_name} + {$M>/detail/last_name} → formatter returns full name string. Expression Inline calculated value. No formatter function needed. Supports ternary operators and comparisons. Always one-way. Properties tab → dsrc field (starts with {= ...}) {= ${$M>/detail/is_escalated} === true ? 'Escalated' : 'Normal'} ⚠ Path and Parts are mutually exclusive on the same property — you cannot use both at once. If you need multiple values combined, always use Parts.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part A — Data Bindings In Depth

documents.t: Path binding wires one control property to one model property. This is the most common binding type for form fields. # Action Detail 1 Select the control in the tree Example: select the complaint_desc m.Input control inside s_complaint_details section. 2 Open Properties tab Detail panel (right side) → Properties tab. 4 Enter the binding in dsrc Type: {$M>/detail/complaint_desc} — the detail TransNode relationId followed by the property ID. 5 Save and verify in Full Preview The field loads with the active complaint's description. Edit it and save — the new value persists in the database. 📘 The TransNode relationId is set in the Page Data Model, not the entity name. If your detail TransNode's relationId is complaints_detail, the path is {$M>/complaints_detail/complaint_desc}.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part A — Data Bindings In Depth

documents.t: Use Parts when you need to combine or transform multiple model values into a single display string. Parts binding is one-way only — it cannot write back to the model. Value​ The value field will hold the value provided for the property. Path​ In this path field, users can only bind with exactly one property or value. This can be used if there is only one property to bind. Parts​ In this path field, users can bind multiple properties or values. This can be used if multiple values or properties need to be provided for binding. (Note: If we are using formatter function, then it is mandatory to provide either parts or path value) Formatter Functions​ Controller function name (formatter function) can be given for the field. Type​ In the type field, the user can provide the datatype for the control’s value. Formatter Options​ Formatter options define how a value is formatted and displayed in the UI. Validation Constraint​ Constraints are optional and define how an input value that is entered in the UI should look like. During parsing, the value is validated against these constraints. For example, an Integer type has a constraint for the maximum that is automatically validated when parsing the input values. Example: displaying TAT status as a composite string from actual_tat and standard_tat. // Controller function — formatTAT public formatTAT(actual: number, standard: number): string { if (!actual || !standard) return '—'; const diff = actual - standard; if (diff <= 0) return `✅ On Time (${actual} days)`; return `⚠ Overdue by ${diff} day(s) — Actual: ${actual}, SLA: ${standard}`; } ⚠ The formatter function receives Part values in the exact order they appear in the Parts list. If you add actual_tat first and standard_tat second, the function signature must be formatTAT(actual, standard).
documents.s: A.4 — Parts Binding with Formatter Function
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part A — Data Bindings In Depth

documents.t: Expression binding lets you write a JavaScript ternary expression directly inside a binding path string. It starts with {= and ends with }. It is evaluated live at runtime whenever the bound model values change.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part B — Expression Bindings

documents.t: Rule Detail Starts with {= The expression must begin with {= (curly brace, equals). Without the =, it is treated as a plain path, not an expression. Reference model paths with ${} Inside an expression, wrap every $M path in ${}: ${$M>/detail/s_status}. This dereferences the path to its current value. Must return a value The expression must evaluate to a value matching the property type. visible expects boolean. text expects string. enabled expects boolean. Ternary only for simple cases Use condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse. Complex multi-branch logic belongs in a formatter function, not in expression binding. No function calls You cannot call controller functions from expression binding. Use Parts + formatter for that.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part B — Expression Bindings

documents.t: Use Case Property Expression Explanation Show Save/Cancel only in EDIT or CREATE mode visible {= ${$M>/TransactionMode } === 'EDIT' || ${$M>/TransactionMode } === 'CREATE' ? true : false} screenMode is a system property on every screen. It switches to EDIT when setMode is called. Make Edit button invisible in EDIT mode visible {= ${$M>/TransactionMode } === 'DISPLAY' ? true : false} Edit button should disappear the moment the user clicks it and mode switches to EDIT. Show escalation badge only when escalated visible {= ${$M>/detail/is_escalated} === true ? true : false} is_escalated is a Boolean property. Bind to the is_escalated path directly. Dynamic text: 'Escalated' vs empty text {= ${$M>/detail/is_escalated} === true ? 'ESCALATED' : ''} Shows ESCALATED label text conditionally. Returns empty string otherwise. Disable complaint_desc when not OPEN enabled {= ${$M>/detail/s_status} === 'OPEN' ? true : false} The complaint description should only be editable when the complaint is in OPEN status. Dynamic placeholder label for priority text {= ${$M>/detail/priority} === 'VERY_HIGH' ? '🚨 Critical' : ${$M>/detail/priority}} Shows emoji label for critical priority, falls back to raw value for others. TAT warning color class {= ${$M>/detail/actual_tat} > ${$M>/detail/standard_tat} ? 'tat-overdue' : 'tat-ok'} Applies different CSS class depending on whether actual exceeds standard TAT. ⚠ Expression binding is evaluated once per model change event. For heavy computation (e.g. comparing arrays or doing date math), use a formatter function instead — expression binding performance degrades with complex logic.
documents.s: B.2 — Expression Binding Examples (Customer Complaints App)
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part B — Expression Bindings

documents.t: A formatter function is a TypeScript method in the controller file that takes one or more raw model values as input and returns a formatted display value. It is the right tool whenever expression binding would become too long, needs multi-step logic, or needs to look up external data.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part C — Formatter Functions

documents.t: Formatter functions are public methods on the controller class. They must be public — the framework calls them reflectively from the Page Builder binding. export class p_complaints extends KloController { // Formatter functions — called from Parts binding in Page Builder public formatPriority(priority: string): string { const map: Record<string,string> = { 'LOW': '🟢 Low', 'MEDIUM': '🟡 Medium', 'HIGH': '🔴 High', 'VERY_HIGH': '🚨 Very High' }; return map[priority] || priority || '—'; } }
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part C — Formatter Functions

documents.t: Function Name Input Parts Return Example Output formatPriority(priority) {$M>/detail/priority} string 🔴 High formatTAT(actual, standard) {$M>/detail/actual_tat}, {$M>/detail/standard_tat} string ⚠ Overdue by 3 day(s) formatStatusLabel(status) {$M>/detail/s_status} string 🟠 IN PROCESS formatFullName(first, last) {$M>/detail/created_by_first}, {$M>/detail/created_by_last} string John Doe formatEscalationText(isEsc, type) {$M>/detail/is_escalated}, {$M>/detail/complaint_type} string ESCALATED — BILLING formatDateAge(createdOn) {$M>/detail/created_on} string 3 days ago
documents.s: C.2 — Formatter Function Examples for the Complaints App
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part C — Formatter Functions

documents.t: # Action Detail 1 Write the function in controller.ts Open the controller file in Code Browser. Add a public method with the formatter logic. Ensure it takes the exact number of parameters as the number of Parts you will add. 2 Select the target control Page Builder → select the control whose display property you want to format (e.g. m.Text for priority display). 3 Delete existing Path binding If a Path binding exists on the property, clear it first — Parts and Path cannot coexist. 4 Switch to Parts Properties tab → click Parts radio button. 5 Add each Part in order Click + for each model path. Order matters: Part 1 = first function argument, Part 2 = second argument, etc. 6 Set Formatter Function field Type the exact function name as it appears in the controller. No parentheses, no 'this.' prefix. 7 Private Node must be running Formatter function calls go to the running Private Node. Start your Private Node before testing. Without it, the binding silently returns undefined. 8 Save and Full Preview The control should now render formatted output. Open Chrome DevTools Sources to debug if the output is wrong. ⚠ Formatter functions must be PURE — they should not modify model state, call APIs, or have side effects. They are called repeatedly on every model refresh. Side effects cause unpredictable behavior and performance issues.
documents.s: C.3 — Wiring a Formatter Function: Complete Steps

documents.t: Navigation in Klobase is handled exclusively through the navTo() controller API. All legacy navigation methods (navToS, navToByEvent, navToScreenByKeyScreen) are deprecated — always use navTo. It is defined on KloController and is available in every page controller via this.navTo().
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part D — Navigation In Depth

documents.t: Parameter Type Purpose Example SS string Navigate to a section (PageArea or Section) WITHIN the same page. Used for list-to-detail navigation on the same screen. SS: 'pa_complaint_details' S string Navigate to a DIFFERENT page by page ID. S: 'p_customers' D string Navigate to a page AND set a specific record as active by its primary key. Format: entity@@key@@suffix. D: 'd_complaints@@CMP-00012@@F' QP object Navigate to a page AND apply a query parameter filter on the target page's search TransNode. QP: { complaint_type: 'BILLING' } F string Navigate to a specific flavor (application variant). F: 'flavor_prod' Mode string Set the page mode on the target page when navigating. Values: DISPLAY, EDIT, CREATE. Mode: 'CREATE' AppData object Pass arbitrary data to the target page. Read from controller using this.getAppData(). AppData: { source: 'dashboard' }
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part D — Navigation In Depth

documents.t: Scenario 1 — List row click navigates to detail section on the same page: // Press event on ticket_id m.Link control: await this.navTo({ SS: 'pa_complaint_details' }, oEvent); // oEvent is required for SS nav — it carries the row index for setActive Scenario 2 — Navigate to a different page: await this.navTo({ S: 'p_customers' }); Scenario 3 — Navigate to a different page AND a specific section within it: await this.navTo({ S: 'p_customers', SS: 'pa_customer_details' }, oEvent); Scenario 4 — Navigate to a page and load a specific record by key (requires navbykey on target TransNode): const key = this.tm.getTN('list').getProperty(`${idx}/complaint_id`); await this.navTo({ S: 'p_complaints', SS: 'pa_complaint_details', D: `d_complaints@@${key}@@F` }); // Target page's detail TransNode must have navbykey: {"sourcePath": "list"} Scenario 5 — Navigate and pre-filter with query parameters (requires navbyquery on target TransNode): const type = this.tm.getTN('detail').getProperty('complaint_type'); await this.navTo({ S: 'p_complaints', SS: 'pa_complaints', QP: { complaint_type: type } }); // Target page's search TransNode must have navbyquery: {"sourcePath": "search"} Scenario 6 — Navigate to Create mode on a different page: await this.navTo({ S: 'p_complaints', Mode: 'CREATE' });
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part D — Navigation In Depth

documents.t: Config Field Where to Set Value Format When Required navbykey Target page's detail/list TransNode → Properties → navbykey field {"sourcePath": "list"} — the list TransNode relationId of the TARGET page Required when using D: parameter in navTo. It tells the target page which TransNode to activate. navbyquery Target page's search TransNode → Properties → navbyquery field {"sourcePath": "search"} — the search TransNode relationId of the TARGET page Required when using QP: parameter in navTo. It tells the target page to filter using the passed query params.

documents.t: The Style Classes tab in the Page Builder is the single place to control all visual formatting. It has two modes: QuickAdd (pre-built bundles) and Manual (full control). Different QuickAdd bundles are available depending on what is selected in the tree: a Section, a PageArea/PageLayout, or a Control.
documents.s: Part E — Style Classes for Controls, Sections, Page Areas & Layouts
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part E — Style Classes for Controls, Sections, Page Areas & Layouts

documents.t: QuickAdd Style Applied On What It Does When to Use Card Sections (form/detail type) Adds a white background, rounded corners, drop shadow, and inner padding. Renders the section as a card floating above the page. Detail form sections (s_detail_header, s_complaint_details). Makes key information stand out. Grid Sections (grid type) Adds alternating row colors, column borders, header background, and hover highlight. Improves readability for dense tabular data. List sections (s_complaints). Always apply Grid QuickAdd to any grid-type section. Transparent Sections Removes background and border. Content sits directly on the page background. Dashboard tile sections where background should show through.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part E — Style Classes for Controls, Sections, Page Areas & Layouts

documents.t: QuickAdd Style Applied On What It Does Font Size (S/M/L/XL) m.Text, m.Label, m.Input Applies a pre-defined font size class. Use L for emphasis, S for secondary information in grid cells. Text Colour Any text control Applies a branded color from the platform color palette. Includes: primary (blue), success (green), warning (orange), danger (red). Bold m.Text, m.Label Applies font-weight: bold. Use for headers, primary identifiers (complaint_id), and totals. Italic m.Text Applies font-style: italic. Use for secondary metadata (timestamps, remarks). Background Color Any control Applies a background highlight. Useful for dashboard tiles and key metrics. Color Combination Any control Pre-defined foreground + background pairs ensuring WCAG contrast compliance. Safer than picking colors individually.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part E — Style Classes for Controls, Sections, Page Areas & Layouts

documents.t: Format Rules apply a style class conditionally based on the control's current value. This is how status badge colors work. Configure via Style Classes tab → Category + Style Class + Format Rule + Format Value. Field What It Does Example Category What CSS property the rule affects: Background, Text, or Icon. Background Style Class The CSS class name to apply when the condition is true. status-open Format Rule The condition type: Text Contains, Text Equals, Text Starts With, etc. Text Contains Format Value The value of the control's text must match for the class to apply. OPEN Full Row When checked, the style applies to the entire grid row instead of just the cell. Checked for critical priority rows that need full-row coloring. Status badge rules for the complaints app — apply to s_status control in both s_complaints grid and s_detail_header: Status Value Category Style Class Format Rule Format Value OPEN Background status-open Text Contains OPEN REOPEN Background status-reopen Text Contains REOPEN INPROCESS Background status-inprocess Text Contains INPROCESS ON_HOLD Background status-onhold Text Contains ON_HOLD RESOLVED Background status-resolved Text Contains RESOLVED CLOSED Background status-completed Text Contains CLOSED
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part E — Style Classes for Controls, Sections, Page Areas & Layouts

documents.t: When QuickAdd and Format Rules are not sufficient, create custom CSS classes in the System Settings. # Action Detail 1 category Select category as user defined 2 Style class Provide your own style class 3 Add css file Maintain css file in css folder 4 Load file in controller FileLoaderUtils.loadCSSFile(this.getFlavor(), this.getFlavorVersion(), "myStyleSheet"); "myStyleSheet" this is the style sheet has been created
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part E — Style Classes for Controls, Sections, Page Areas & Layouts

documents.t: Recommendation ✓ ✓ Use Style Classes first. Use Category + Style Class + Format Rule (Quick Add ) before creating a custom CSS file(user defined). ✓ ✓ Scope custom CSS to the flavor. Wrap CSS rules in .procify__<app_id> { ... }, using the flavor name without the version. ✓ ✓ Load CSS in onpageInit(). Use FileLoaderUtils.loadCSSFile(this.getFlavor(), this.getFlavorVersion(), "myStyleSheet");. ✓ ✓ Use SAPUI5/OpenUI5 classes. Target classes such as .sapMIBar, .sapUiTableRow, .sapMTB, and .KloTabContainerHeaderToolbar. ✓ ✓ Test across supported platforms. Verify custom CSS on APK, IPA, Safari, and Chrome before releasing it. ✓ ✓ Use :has() for whole-grid-cell styling. Add a User Defined class to the control and use td:has(.yourClassName) { ... } when the entire cell must be styled. ✓ ✓ Check layout configuration first. For height, spacing, or positioning issues, check screenType options such as fit_to_area, hsplitter, vsplitter, and grid_layout before overriding CSS. ✓ ✓ Order Format Rules carefully. Place general rules first and more-specific rules later when values can overlap.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 6 — Bindings, Navigation & Styling/Part E — Style Classes for Controls, Sections, Page Areas & Layouts

documents.t: Avoid ✗ ✗ Don’t use unsupported Format Rule types. Only Always, Text Contains, and Formula are supported. ✗ ✗ Don’t use overlapping Text Contains values without checking the order. For example, OPEN also matches REOPEN. ✗ ✗ Don’t expect CSS to inherit between flavors. A child flavor must load its own stylesheet. ✗ ✗ Don’t assume embedded screens inherit CSS. Each screen must load the CSS it requires. ✗ ✗ Don’t modify Shared flavor CSS without checking the current access policy. Confirm with the platform team before making changes. ✗ ✗ Don’t use Style Class alone to color an entire grid cell. It styles the control inside the cell, not the <td>. ✗ ✗ Don’t leave the Style Class field empty. An empty Style Class prevents the style from being applied. ✗ ✗ Don’t hardcode custom class names in multiple places. Once loaded, the class is available under Category: User Defined in the Style Class UI. Reuse that class instead.

Controller function body Vienable — Role Visibility by role ID: EMPLOYEE, EMPLOYEE_MANAGER, IT_TEAM. Vienable Dashboard → Role column Vienable — Status Group Visibility by status group: OPEN, INPROCESS, ACCEPTED, COMPLETED. documents.t: Vienable (Visible + Enable) is the declarative system for controlling control visibility and editability across four independent dimensions. The final result for any control is the intersection of all configured dimensions: a control is visible only if ALL applicable dimension rules say it should be visible.
documents.s: Part A — Vienable: Complete Configuration Guide
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 7 — Controllers & Client-Side Behaviour/Part A — Vienable Complete Configuration Guide

documents.t: Dimension What It Controls Values Configuration Location Page Size Visibility/enable by device screen resolution. Evaluated based on the PARENT section's resolved size. S (phone), M (tablet), L (desktop), XL (wide desktop) Vienable Dashboard → Page Size columns: S, M, L, XL Page Mode Visibility/enable by current screen interaction mode. Default mode is DISPLAY. Display, Edit, Create, Review Vienable Dashboard → Page Mode columns Role Visibility/enable by the logged-in user's s_role_rollup value. Config must be maintained in Procify Data Studio → Object Type tab. Owner (10), Supervisor (20), Reviewer (30), Overlooker (40). In this app: EMPLOYEE=10, EMPLOYEE_MANAGER=20, IT_TEAM=30 Vienable Dashboard → Role column Status Group Visibility/enable by the bound entity's current s_status_group value. Config must be maintained in Procify Data Studio → Status tab. The Status Groups you defined in Session 3. In this app: OPEN, INPROCESS, ACCEPTED, COMPLETED Vienable Dashboard → Status Group column ⚠ Entity must be set to TRUE for the control row in the Vienable Dashboard. If Entity = false, Role and Status Group dimensions are ignored — the control will always be visible/enabled regardless of role or status.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 7 — Controllers & Client-Side Behaviour/Part A — Vienable Complete Configuration Guide

documents.t: Screen size Vienable controls which columns/fields appear on small vs large screens. This is how the platform supports mobile without a separate build. Page Size Approx. Viewport Recommended for Complaints App S Up to ~600px (phone) Show only: ticket_id (link), priority, s_status. Hide: complaint_desc, customer_id, dates, responsible_team. M 601–1024px (tablet) Show: ticket_id, priority, s_status, complaint_type. Still hide verbose date columns. L 1025–1440px (desktop) Show all columns. Standard desktop experience. XL Above 1440px (wide desktop) Same as L. Use for additional panel layout or expanded detail. Steps to configure phone layout for s_complaints grid: # Action Detail 1 Open Vienable Dashboard Page Builder → p_complaints page → Vienable tab → Vienable Dashboard sub-tab. 2 Set Entity = true for each grid column control Find complaint_desc, customer_id, first_response_date, responsible_team in the Control ID column. Toggle Entity to true. 3 Set S column = Hidden for verbose columns For each verbose column: click the S (phone) cell → set to Hidden (🚫 icon). 4 Keep S = Visible for essential columns ticket_id, priority, s_status: ensure S is set to Visible (👁 icon). 5 Test with Preview In → Phone Toolbar → Preview In → Phone. Grid should show only the essential 3 columns. 6 Verify desktop unaffected Preview In → Desktop. All columns must still show.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 7 — Controllers & Client-Side Behaviour/Part A — Vienable Complete Configuration Guide

documents.t: Control Display Mode Edit Mode Create Mode Rationale Edit button Visible Hidden Hidden Edit disappears when clicked (mode switches to EDIT). Save button Hidden Visible Visible Only meaningful when there is something to save. Cancel button Hidden Visible Visible Only meaningful when there is something to discard. documents.t: Role-based Vienable uses the s_role_rollup value of the logged-in user. This value is set in Procify Data Studio → Object Type tab → role configuration table (KloTuner config). The mapping for this is: Application Role Procify Role s_role_rollup Vienable Role ID Employee Owner 10 EMPLOYEE Manager Supervisor 20 EMPLOYEE_MANAGER Responsible Team Reviewer 30 IT_TEAM Role-based Vienable rules for p_complaints — key controls: Control EMPLOYEE EMPLOYEE_MANAGER IT_TEAM Delete button (toolbar) Hidden Visible (OPEN group only) Hidden responsible_team field (EDIT) Show As Label Editable Show As Label complaint_desc field (EDIT) Editable (OPEN group only) Show As Label Show As Label assigned_to field (EDIT) Show As Label Editable Show As Label remark field (EDIT) Hidden Editable Editable

documents.t: Status Group maps a set of s_status values to a group name. The configuration is in Procify Data Studio → Status tab. Vienable evaluates the group of the entity's CURRENT s_status to decide visibility. Status Group Name Statuses It Covers Typical Vienable Use OPEN OPEN, REOPEN Edit button visible. complaint_desc editable for EMPLOYEE. INPROCESS INPROCESS, ON_HOLD Edit button visible. Assign team button available for MANAGER. ACCEPTED RESOLVED Edit button hidden — complaint resolved, no edits allowed. COMPLETED CLOSED Edit button hidden — complaint closed. Only the Reopen button is shown. ⚠ Status Group Vienable requires Entity = true on the control row AND the entity's Status tab must have the groups configured in Procify Data Studio. Missing group config causes the status group column to be ignored — the control remains visible regardless of status.

documents.t: The Klobase framework calls lifecycle hook methods on your controller class at specific points in the page's life. Understanding WHEN each fires is essential — using the wrong hook causes bugs that are hard to trace because they appear intermittently depending on navigation order.
documents.s: Part B — Controller Page Lifecycle Hooks
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 7 — Controllers & Client-Side Behaviour/Part B — Controller Page Lifecycle Hooks

documents.t: On first page load: onPageInit → onPageModelReady → onPageEnter On forward navigation back to same page: onPageEnter (only) On backward navigation away from page: onPageExit (source page), onPageEnter (target page) On back-navigation that destroys the page: onPageExit → onPageDestroy
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 7 — Controllers & Client-Side Behaviour/Part B — Controller Page Lifecycle Hooks

documents.t: Hook When It Fires Model Data Available? Primary Use Cases Common Mistakes onPageInit Once, when controller class loads. UI, model, and TransNodes do NOT exist yet. No Rare: one-time non-model setup like subscribing to a global service. Trying to access this.tm or TransNodes — they are null at this point. onPageModelReady Once (per page lifecycle), after TransNodes are initialized but BEFORE data is fetched. No (TransNodes exist but have no data) Call this.tm.getTN('search').skipModelPreparation() to skip auto-query execution and manually control data load. Reading TransNode data — getData() returns null or empty. The fetch hasn't happened yet. onPageEnter Every time the page becomes visible — forward nav, backward nav, and initial load. Yes Dashboard count calculations. Resetting UI state. Refreshing summaries. Setting default filter values. Putting logic that should only run ONCE here — it re-runs on every navigation. Use _initialized flag for one-time logic. onPageExit When the user navigates AWAY to a different page. Yes Auto-save draft, log exit event, clear unsaved state. Not called for within-page section navigation (SS). Only fires on cross-page navigation. onPageDestroy Once, when the page is removed from memory (back-nav that exits the page history). Partially Unsubscribe event listeners. Release resources. Not needed for most standard screens. Using it as a reliable 'save on exit' hook — the page may be destroyed without user navigation (memory pressure, app backgrounding).
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 7 — Controllers & Client-Side Behaviour/Part B — Controller Page Lifecycle Hooks

documents.t: onPageEnter is the page lifecycle hook. It fires with data already loaded, on every navigation — making it perfect for dashboard counts, summaries, and state resets. This event will be called whenever the screen enters the visible area by means of navigation (Both front and back navigation). public async onPageEnter(): Promise<void> { // ── 1. One-time initialization guard ────────────────────────────────── if (!this._initialized) { this._initialized = true; // Logic that must run only ONCE goes here } // ── 2. Dashboard count computation (server-side aggregate) ──────────── // "status_count_query" = a query-type transnode configured with: // SELECT s_status, COUNT(k_ticket_id) AS count_of_status // FROM <entity> WHERE <same filters as before> GROUP BY s_status const countQueryTN = this.tm.getTN('status_count_query').getData(); const aggregateResult = await countQueryTN.executeP(); const rows = aggregateResult; const counts: Record<string, number> = { OPEN: 0, REOPEN: 0, INPROCESS: 0, ON_HOLD: 0, RESOLVED: 0, CLOSED: 0 }; rows.forEach((row: any) => { const st = row.s_status || ''; const c = Number(row.count_of_status) || 0; if (counts.hasOwnProperty(st)) counts[st] = c; }); // Build the derived object once, then set it on a dedicated // "other"-type transnode used purely for binding — no full row payload involved. const statusCount = { t_open_count: counts.OPEN + counts.REOPEN, t_inprocess_count: counts.INPROCESS + counts.ON_HOLD, t_resolved_count: counts.RESOLVED, t_closed_count: counts.CLOSED }; await this.tm.getTN('status_count').setData(statusCount); }
documents.s: B.3 — onPageEnter: The Most Important Hook

documents.t: API Signature Returns Description getTN() this.tm.getTN(relationId: string) TransNode Get a TransNode by its relationId (as configured in Page Data Model). The gateway to all TransNode operations. commitP() this.tm.commitP(success, failure, validate, isDisplayMode) Promise<any> Save all dirty objects in the Transaction Model to the database. validate=true triggers OnValidate. isDisplayMode=true resets to DISPLAY after save. rollBackTxn() this.tm.rollBackTxn() Promise<void> Revert ALL unsaved changes across all TransNodes back to last commit state. Used by Cancel button. getAllTransNodes() this.tm.getAllTransNodes() TransNode[] Get all TransNodes on the page. Useful for bulk operations. getTransactionFromTransnodeData() this.tm.getTransactionFromTransnodeData(tn) any Get the raw transaction object from a TransNode. Advanced use only.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 7 — Controllers & Client-Side Behaviour/Part C — Controller APIs Complete Reference

documents.t: API Signature Returns Description & Example getData() .getData() KloEntitySet / KloEntity / KloQuery Get all data from the TransNode. For list TransNodes returns the full entity set. Call .toArray() on the result to iterate. data = this.tm.getTN('list').getData(); getActiveData() .getActiveData() KloEntity Get only the currently active (selected/highlighted) entity. data = this.tm.getTN('detail').getActiveData(); getProperty() .getProperty(path: string) any Get a single property value from the TransNode model. For list rows: getProperty('0/complaint_id') — index/propertyId format. For detail: getProperty('complaint_desc'). setProperty() .setProperty(path, value) TransNode Set a property value — triggers immediate UI re-render. For transient/display properties. setProperty('t_open_count', '5'). setData() .setData(val, index?) Promise<void> Set the entire dataset for a TransNode. Replaces current data. Used after manual data fetch. this.tm.getTN('list').setData(entitySet); setActive() .setActive(index) Promise<bool> Set the active row by index. Triggers onArrive and updates all child TransNodes. await this.tm.getTN('list').setActive(0); getActiveIndex() .getActiveIndex() number Get the current active row index. Useful before navigating away. idx = this.tm.getTN('list').getActiveIndex(); getSelectedEntities() .getSelectedEntities(ssID?) KloEntity[] Get all checked rows in a grid section (multi-select). selected = this.tm.getTN('list').getSelectedEntities(); executeP() .executeP() Promise<void> Re-execute the query associated with a query-type TransNode. Use to refresh data without full page reload. await this.tm.getTN('search').executeP(); applySortP() .applySortP(property, order) Promise<void> Sort the TransNode data by a property. order: 'ASCENDING' or 'DESCENDING'. await this.tm.getTN('list').applySortP('created_on', 'DESCENDING'); createEntityP() .createEntityP(json, successMsg, errorMsg) Promise<KloEntity> Create a new entity and add to the TransNode. Triggers onAfterCreate hook server-side. await this.tm.getTN('list').createEntityP({complaint_desc: 'test'}, 'Created', 'Failed');

documents.t: API Signature Description navTo() await this.navTo(params, oEvent?) Navigate to section or page. See Part D of Session 6 for full parameter reference. setMode() this.setMode('EDIT' | 'DISPLAY' | 'CREATE') Set the screen mode for all TransNodes bound to the detail area. Used by Edit button press event. saveTransaction() this.saveTransaction(successMsg, errorMsg, validate, resetMode) Commit dirty data, optionally trigger OnValidate, and optionally reset to DISPLAY. Standard Save button handler. refreshTransnode() this.refreshTransnode(nodeId, mode, discard) Refresh a named TransNode, set its mode, and optionally discard unsaved changes. Standard Cancel button handler. showBusy() this.showBusy(msg?, id?) Show the platform busy/loading indicator. Use during async operations. this.showBusy('Loading...'); hideBusy() this.hideBusy(id?) Hide the busy indicator. Always call in a finally block to ensure it's dismissed even on error. getAppData() this.getAppData() Retrieve AppData passed from the source page's navTo call. Returns the object passed as AppData: {...}. getPathFromEvent() this.getPathFromEvent(oEvent) Get the model path string from a press event. Use with getTN().getProperty(path.split('/')[2] + '/propertyId') to get a specific row value.

documents.t: Client-side validation in Klobase operates at two levels: (1) field-level required constraints using the 'required' property, and (2) full-form OnValidate triggered by commitP or saveTransaction. Both are enforced in the browser before any network call is made.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 7 — Controllers & Client-Side Behaviour/Part D — Client-Side Validation

documents.t: Mark a control as required by adding the 'required' property and setting it to true. The platform renders a red asterisk and prevents submission if the field is empty. # Action Detail 1 Select the input control Page Builder → select the mandatory field control, e.g. complaint_desc m.Input. 2 Add 'required' property Properties tab → Add → required → set Value to true. 3 Test in Full Preview (CREATE mode) Click New → leave complaint_desc empty → click Save. Platform shows required validation error and blocks save.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 7 — Controllers & Client-Side Behaviour/Part D — Client-Side Validation

documents.t: OnValidate runs in the entity file (.ts) on the Private Node when saveTransaction is called with validate=true. The client sends the dirty object to the server; the server validates and returns errors if any rule fails. The client then displays these errors as message dialogs. // In d_complaints.ts entity file — OnValidate hook public async OnValidate(oEvent: IKloEvent): Promise<void> { const entity = oEvent.getEntity(); const errors: string[] = []; // V001: Description must be at least 20 characters if (!entity.complaint_desc || entity.complaint_desc.length < 20) { errors.push('V001: Complaint description must be at least 20 characters.'); } // V002: Priority is mandatory if (!entity.priority) { errors.push('V002: Priority is mandatory.'); } // V003: Cannot close without a remark if (entity.s_status === 'CLOSED' && !entity.remark) { errors.push('V003: Remark is required when closing a complaint.'); } if (errors.length > 0) { oEvent.setError(errors.join('\n')); } } For OnValidate to fire from the UI, the detail TransNode's setActiveIf must be set to 'Valid' in the Page Data Model. Without this, saveTransaction with validate=true does nothing. # Action Detail 1 Set setActiveIf on detail TransNode Page Data Model → click detail TransNode → setActiveIf dropdown → select Valid. 2 Call saveTransaction with validate=true Edit button press: this.setMode('EDIT'). Save button press: this.saveTransaction('Saved.', 'Save failed.', true, true). 3 Test validation Leave complaint_desc with fewer than 20 characters → Save → OnValidate fires → error message dialog shows V001 text. 4 Fix and retry Enter a valid description → Save → passes validation → data persists → mode resets to DISPLAY.
documents.s: D.2 — OnValidate (Server-Side Validation Triggered from Client)

documents.t: These standards are non-negotiable on all Procify projects. Violations result in code review rejection and technical debt. The principles come from kloTouch 7.0 Basic Training Guide §7.4 and §7.5.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 7 — Controllers & Client-Side Behaviour/Part E — Coding Standards

documents.t: Rule Do Don't Reason Scope Write ONLY UI logic in the controller: formatters, navigation, show/hide, model reads for display. Write business logic (status transitions, validations, default-setting) in the controller. Business logic in the controller bypasses server validation and breaks when the screen is accessed via API. TypeScript typing Declare every variable with its type: const count: number = 0; const msg: string = ''; Use implicit any: let x = someValue; or omit types on function parameters. Untyped code hides bugs at compile time that surface as runtime errors in production. Variable declaration Declare variables only when necessary. Prefer const over let. Declare variables at file scope (class properties) when a local variable suffices. File-scope variables persist across page navigations and cause state leakage between sessions. Nested functions Keep functions flat. Extract complex logic to named private methods. Nest arrow functions inside controller methods: onClick(() => { const x = () => {...}; }) Nested functions are not testable, not readable, and difficult to debug. Async/await Use async/await for all TransNode API calls. Mark the function async. Use .then().catch() promise chains. Consistent await pattern is required by the framework for proper error propagation. Deprecated APIs Always use navTo(), tm.commitP(), this.setMode(). Use navToS(), navToByEvent(), getTN('x').commitP() Deprecated APIs are removed in future versions. Using them creates upgrade risk. Model mutation Only modify model properties via setProperty() for transient display values. Directly mutate entity properties from the controller (entity.some_prop = value). Direct mutations bypass the dirty-tracking mechanism and do not persist on save.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 7 — Controllers & Client-Side Behaviour/Part E — Coding Standards

documents.t: Rule Do Don't Scope Write ONLY business logic in entity files: onCreate defaults, onUpdate role checks, onDelete restrictions, beforeQ filtering, OnValidate. Write navigation or UI state changes in entity files. Setter functions Use setter override pattern to automatically derive related values when a property changes. Compute derived values in the controller on button press — this is bypassed when data changes via API. Validation location All mandatory field checks and business rule violations go in OnValidate. Throw errors in onAfterCreate — onAfterCreate is called AFTER the record is saved; errors there cause data inconsistency. Error handling Always wrap async BOL API calls (createEntityP, LoadEntityByKeyP) in try/catch and log errors. Let unhandled promise rejections propagate silently. Role checks in rules Use oEvent.getTxn().$SYSTEM.roleID to get the runtime role and enforce role-specific logic. Hardcode user IDs or email addresses for role checks.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 7 — Controllers & Client-Side Behaviour/Part E — Coding Standards

documents.t: Item Convention Example Pages p_ prefix + snake_case description p_complaints, p_complaint_dashboard Page Areas pa_ prefix pa_complaint_details, pa_complaints Sections s_ prefix s_complaints, s_detail_header Entities d_ prefix d_complaints, d_complaint_item Queries q_ prefix q_complaints, q_customers Transient properties t_ prefix t_open_count, t_selected_count Controller functions (formatters) format + PascalCase formatPriority, formatTAT, formatStatusLabel Controller functions (event handlers) on + PascalCase + action onEditPress, onSavePress, onDeleteConfirm Variables in TypeScript camelCase + explicit type const openCount: number = 0; Boolean variables is/has prefix isEscalated, hasAttachment, isLoading ⚠ Private Node must be running whenever you test controller functions, formatter functions, or OnValidate. Without the Private Node, server-side hooks are bypassed and the client shows incorrect results. Always verify Private Node status in the App Builder toolbar before testing.

documents.t: Concept What It Does Where to Configure Navigation Designer (Menu Builder) Defines hamburger menu structure. Roles blank = all users. NO hyphens in Menu ID. App Builder → Navigation Designer → select app → Edit Header + Child Item Header groups child menu items visually. Children point to actual screens. Navigation Designer → Add → Add Header, then Add → Add Child sap-icon:// SAP UI5 icon URI format used in menu and controls. Navigation Designer → Menu Icon field HomePage Editor Adds tiles to the Home (🏠) grid. Separate from Landing Page. App Builder → HomePage Editor Landing Page Settings Sets auto-load screen after login. Configured in Session 5. App Builder → Landing Page Settings App Status: RELEASED Locks development. Enables transport. New version must be created from RELEASED. Procify Workspace Hub → My Apps → Status field Branch Parallel ACTIVE copy for next-phase development. Not transportable directly. Procify Workspace Hub → App Compare & Merge Validate Checks for errors. Safe — nothing deployed. Download XLSX report. documents.t: The Navigation Designer (also called Menu Builder per PROC-26419) is the tool you use to define the navigation structure visible to users in the hamburger menu of the application at runtime. Without a menu entry, users cannot navigate between screens — they would need to know URLs manually. Access path: Running app → Hamburger menu (☰) → App Builder → Navigation Designer.
documents.s: A.1 — What Is the Navigation Designer?
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 8 — App Management, Versioning & Publishing/Part A — Navigation Designer

documents.t: Field Description Rules / Notes Menu ID Unique identifier for this menu item. ONLY alphanumeric + underscores. NO hyphens ( - ). NO spaces. Case-sensitive. Wrong: mn-complaints. Correct: mn_complaints. Target Page Page ID the menu item navigates to. Use the Value Help (VH) icon to pick from existing pages. Do NOT type the page ID manually. Menu Text Label shown to the user in the hamburger menu. Keep it short. Title case. Localisation supported. Page Parameters Optional JSON for navTo params (SS, QP, D, Mode). Leave blank for simple page nav. Not needed for the Complaints entry. Menu Icon SAP icon URI displayed alongside the text. Format: sap-icon://<icon-name>. Must be a valid SAP UI5 icon name. Example: sap-icon://customer-and-contacts. Sequence Sort order in the menu. Lower number = appears first. Use multiples of 10 (10, 20, 30) to leave room for future items. Roles Restrict visibility to specific application roles. Leave BLANK = visible to ALL roles. Fill role IDs (comma-separated) to restrict. Test Navigation Validates the menu item navigates correctly. Always click Test Navigation before saving — catches target page errors early.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 8 — App Management, Versioning & Publishing/Part A — Navigation Designer

documents.t: Menu Field Value Menu ID mn_complaints Target Page p_complaints (select from VH) Menu Text Complaints Menu Icon sap-icon://customer-and-contacts Sequence 10 Roles Leave blank — visible to ALL roles (Employee, Manager, IT Team) Page Parameters Not required — leave blank

documents.t: 1 Open Navigation Designer In the running application, open the hamburger menu (☰ top-left). Go to App Builder → Navigation Designer. 2 Select the Application In the App dropdown at the top of the Navigation Designer, select customer_complaints_<prid>. Click the Edit button (pencil icon ✏). The menu table becomes editable. 3 Add a Header Group Click Add (+) → Add Header. Fill in: Menu ID: hdr_main Menu Text: Main Sequence: 10 Roles: leave blank Click OK. (A Header groups child items visually in the menu.) 4 Add the Complaints Child Menu Item Select the hdr_main row in the table. Click Add (+) → Add Child. Fill in: Menu ID: mn_complaints Target Page: p_complaints (use VH picker) Menu Text: Complaints Menu Icon: sap-icon://customer-and-contacts Sequence: 10 Roles: leave blank Click OK. 5 Test the Navigation Click Test Navigation on the mn_complaints row. p_complaints should open correctly. If a 'Page not found' error appears — check that the Target Page is exactly p_complaints (no typos). 6 Save Click the Save button (disk icon 💾). Wait for the busy dialog to close. A success toast confirms the menu is saved. 7 Verify with All Personas Log out and log in separately as emp_<prid>, mgr_<prid>, and it_<prid>. In each session, open the hamburger menu. The 'Complaints' item must be visible and navigate to p_complaints for ALL three test users. ⚠ Important Common Navigation Designer Mistakes Hyphen in Menu ID: mn-complaints causes the item to save but NEVER appear in the app. Always use underscore: mn_complaints. Typing Target Page manually: Always use the VH picker. Manual typos cause silent navigation failures. Saving without testing: Always click 'Test Navigation' before saving. It catches missing pages early. Role restriction accident: If the menu item is set to a specific role, other personas cannot see it. Leave Roles blank for all-role visibility.

documents.t: The HomePage Editor configures which screen tiles appear on the application's built-in Home grid — accessible via the Home (🏠) icon. This is separate from the Landing Page (p_complaint_dashboard configured in Session 5). The Landing Page loads automatically on login. The Home grid gives users tile-based navigation to frequently used screens. 📘 Reference / Tip Three 'home' concepts — don't confuse them Landing Page (Session 5): Configured via Landing Page Settings. Auto-loads after login. Shows p_complaint_dashboard. HomePage Editor: Tile grid shown when user clicks the Home (🏠) icon. Configure p_complaints and p_complaint_dashboard tiles here. p_home_page (BRD): A screen defined in the BRD. Can be built as an additional home screen — not required for this session's delivery.

documents.t: Every version of an application on the Procify platform has a Status that controls what operations are allowed on it. Understanding these statuses is essential before releasing or transporting. Status Meaning Can Develop? Can Transport? Can Create New Version? ACTIVE Current working version. All development happens here. ✅ Yes ❌ No ❌ No RELEASED Development complete and locked. Ready for transport. ❌ No ✅ Yes ✅ Yes (create from RELEASED) DEPRECATED Retired. Superseded by a newer version. ❌ No ❌ No ❌ No DISCARDED Abandoned branch/version. Excluded from main path. ❌ No ❌ No ❌ No ⚠ Important Critical Versioning Rules — memorise these before proceeding A NEW VERSION can only be created from a RELEASED version. A BRANCH can only be created from an ACTIVE version. Branch flavors CANNOT be transported. Merge the branch into a new version first, then transport. Once status is changed to RELEASED, no further development is possible on that version. Always build (Validate & Publish) BEFORE changing status to RELEASED.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Session 8 — App Management, Versioning & Publishing/Part C — App Status Lifecycle & Versioning

documents.t: 1 Navigate to Procify Workspace Hub (also called Workspace Hub) Open the hamburger menu → Deployment Center → Procify Workspace Hub (or Workspace Hub). Alternatively: Hamburger menu → My Apps (if visible in your role). 2 Find Your Application In the Apps list, search for customer_complaints_<prid>. Click the App ID to open the application detail screen. 3 Open Edit Mode Click the Edit button (pencil icon ✏) in the toolbar. The Status field becomes editable. 4 Change Status to RELEASED In the Status dropdown, select RELEASED. Read the confirmation message carefully — this action locks all development on this version. Click Save. The app status changes to RELEASED. The Edit icon in Data Studio and Page Builder will now be disabled for this version. 5 Verify In the App detail, the Status badge shows RELEASED. Open Data Studio → select customer_complaints_<prid> → click the Edit icon. You should see a message that the app is locked for editing.

documents.t: A Branch creates a parallel ACTIVE copy of your application. Use it when you need to work on next-phase enhancements while the current version is being tested in QA. The branch is fully isolated — changes in the branch don't affect the main RELEASED version until you explicitly merge them. Scenario Use Branch? Bug fix on the current version in QA ❌ No — fix directly in main, create new minor version New feature development while current is in QA ✅ Yes — branch from current ACTIVE version Experimental UI changes for client review ✅ Yes — branch lets you show without committing to main

documents.t: 1 Go to Procify Workspace Hub → My Apps Locate customer_complaints_<prid>. The app must be in ACTIVE status to create a branch. 2 Click Branch In the app detail view, click the Branch button (visible only when status = ACTIVE). The platform creates a new Branch Flavor automatically. The branch version appears in the My Apps list with a branch indicator. 3 Assign Users to the Branch Click the branch version to open its detail. Go to the Roles & Users tab → click Edit. Assign ALL three test users and your developer account to their respective roles. ⚠ Users are NOT copied automatically from the parent — you must assign them manually in the branch. 4 Develop in the Branch Open Data Studio or Page Builder. In the App dropdown, select the BRANCH version (not the main version). Make your changes. Save and test independently.

documents.t: When the branch is ready to be merged back into the main release cycle: 1 Export Both ZIPs Procify Workspace Hub → Export section. Download ZIP of the main RELEASED version (Set 1) and the branch version (Set 2). 2 Open App Compare & Merge Procify Workspace Hub → App Compare & Merge. Upload Set 1 (main) as Left and Set 2 (branch) as Right. Click Compare. 3 Review the Differences The tool lists differences per component: entities, pages, queries, VH, menus, etc. For each difference, select which version to keep: Set 1 (main), Set 2 (branch), or a Custom combination. 4 Download Merged ZIP Once all decisions are made, click Download to export the merged ZIP. 5 Create New Version and Import In Procify Workspace Hub, create a new Major or Minor version from the current RELEASED main version. Import the merged ZIP into the new version. Run Update Schema, Full Build, and test before releasing. 📘 Reference / Tip Reference: App Branching & Merging User Guide — App_Branching___Merging-User_Guide.docx PROC-26419 note: 'Procify Workspace Hub' may be renamed 'Workspace Hub' in platform help content. Both names refer to the same tool.

documents.t: Action What It Does When to Use Validate Scans the application for errors WITHOUT building. Safe — nothing changes in the running app. Run first, every time. Fix all errors before triggering Publish. Publish Validates first, then builds the app if no blocking errors exist. Updates the running app. After Validate passes with 0 errors. Use Full Build for first publish or after VH Config changes.
documents.s: E.1 — Validate vs. Publish — What's the Difference?

documents.t: Blocker Cause Fix VH Config not visible in UI after Publish VH Config changes require a Full Build. Always select 'Full Build' for the first publish or after adding/editing VH Configs. TypeScript compilation error Syntax error in entity .ts or controller .ts file. Open VS Code → check terminal for tsc errors → fix, save, re-validate. Update Schema not run Entity properties added but schema not updated in DB. Data Studio → select entity → Update Schema → confirm success toast. Another build IN-QUEUE A previous build is already running. Click 'Proceed' to queue behind the current build. Do NOT cancel it. Missing app_util flavor Build & Deploy menu not visible. Ask trainer — app_util must be assigned to your developer account.

documents.t: 1 Open Build & Deploy Hamburger menu (☰) → App Builder → Build & Deploy. (If this menu item is missing, app_util flavor is not assigned to your account. Ask the trainer.) 2 Enter the Application In the App field, type customer_complaints_<prid> and press Enter. The application version details load. 3 Run Validate First Select Action: Validate. Click Submit. Wait for the validation report to generate. Download the XLSX report if errors are listed. Fix every ERROR before proceeding. Warnings can be reviewed but do not block the build. 4 Fix All Errors For each error in the report: - Missing Update Schema → Data Studio → Update Schema on the entity. - TypeScript error → VS Code → fix tsc error → save → re-validate. - Missing VH Build → select Full Build in the next step. Re-run Validate until the report shows 0 errors. 5 Run Publish Select Action: Publish. Build Type: Full Build (required for first publish and after any VH Config changes). Click Submit. The Publish Log shows the progression: IN-QUEUE → IN-PROCESS → PUBLISHED Do NOT navigate away while the build is running. 6 Verify the Published App Log out completely. Log back in. Open the hamburger menu → confirm 'Complaints' item is visible. Navigate to p_complaints → confirm live data loads. Verify: status badges render, VH dropdowns populate, all tabs in detail section work. 📘 Reference / Tip Build History reference: Publish_Logs_Screen.docx — explains each status stage and error codes. Validate & Publish reference: Publish_or_Validate_Screen-7_0_App_utility__.docx

documents.t: Transport is a PULL mechanism: the TARGET system (QA) asks the SOURCE system (DEV) for the latest published version. You perform ALL transport steps while logged into the QA environment, not DEV. Stage What Happens Setup Transport creates entries in QA metadata tables for the application, groups, and flavors. Download Application ZIPs are pulled from DEV and extracted in the QA server's file system. Update Schema Database tables for all entities are created or altered in the QA database. Finalising Application is set to ACTIVE in QA so users can log in and access it. ⚠ Important Transport Pre-requisites — verify ALL before starting 1. The application must be in RELEASED status on the DEV system. 2. Branch flavors CANNOT be transported. Create a new version, merge, then transport. 3. The QA server's config.json must have mm_klo_online_server pointing to the DEV landscape URL. 4. A host file entry for the DEV system must exist on the QA server. 5. The transport_1 app must be assigned to the developer account on the QA system. If any pre-requisite is missing, the transport will fail at Setup or Download stage. Ask the trainer to verify the QA environment config before proceeding.

documents.t: 1 Log in to the QA System Open the QA environment URL in a browser (trainer provides the URL). Log in with your developer credentials. ⚠ ALL remaining steps are done on QA, not on DEV. 2 Navigate to App Migration Hamburger menu (☰) → Deployment Center → App Migration. The App Migration screen lists all available applications from the connected DEV system. 3 Find Your Application In the list, locate customer_complaints_<prid>. If not visible, toggle the 'Show All' button to see all available apps (not just those with pending updates). 4 Click the App Row Click on customer_complaints_<prid>. A detail panel opens showing available versions from DEV and any already-installed versions in QA. 5 Install As Writable Click the available version update. A dialog appears with two options: As Readable — locked, cannot edit in QA. As Writable — editable, allows continued development in QA. Click 'As Writable' (recommended for training so you can fix issues in QA if needed). 6 Accept Conditions and Proceed A mandatory conditions dialog appears. For each mandatory item (⚠ icon), tick the acceptance checkbox. If prompted about shared flavor movement (on QA/PROD systems), click Proceed. Click Proceed to start the transport. 7 Monitor Transport Stages The screen shows progress through: Setup → Download → Update Schema → Finalising. Wait for each stage to complete. The overall status changes to ACTIVE when done. 8 Assign Users in QA After transport, the app is ACTIVE in QA but has NO users assigned. Go to Procify Workspace Hub → My Apps → customer_complaints_<prid>. Go to Roles & Users tab → assign: emp_<prid> → Employee role mgr_<prid> → Manager role it_<prid> → ResponsibleTeam role Your developer account → Manager role 9 Verify in QA Log out of the QA developer session. Log in as emp_<prid> in QA. Verify: hamburger menu shows 'Complaints', p_complaints loads, all VH dropdowns work. Repeat with mgr_<prid> and it_<prid>. 📘 Reference / Tip Transport User Guide: Transport-_User_Guide.docx The Transport tool supports DEV → QA, QA → PROD, and DEV → DEV movement. Script Library (second tab in Transport screen) shows automated scripts maintained for the system — ask trainer if any scripts need to be run after transport.

documents.t: This smoke test must be completed AFTER publish. It verifies every major feature built across all 8 sessions works correctly in the published application. Run it on DEV first, then repeat on QA after transport. # Persona Action Expected Result 1 EMPLOYEE (emp_<prid>) Login → Menu → Complaints. Click Add (with Object Type = PROCIFY). Fill complaint_desc (10+ chars), priority = HIGH, select customer from picker. Click Save. complaint_id = P-000XX auto-generated. s_status = OPEN. assigned_to = emp_<prid>. Record appears in list. 2 EMPLOYEE Open the new complaint → Edit → Clear complaint_desc → Save. V001 error blocks save: 'Complaint description must be at least 10 characters'. 3 EMPLOYEE Edit → priority dropdown. ComboBox shows Low / Medium / High / Critical (from vhc_priority). 4 EMPLOYEE Edit → customer_id field. F4 picker opens showing d_customers records. 5 MANAGER (mgr_<prid>) Login → open the OPEN complaint → Edit → set responsible_team from picker → Save. responsible_team field is editable for Manager. Record saves. Status remains OPEN. 6 IT TEAM (it_<prid>) Login → open assigned complaint → Edit → s_status = INPROCESS → Save. Status badge changes to INPROCESS (orange colour). Edit button remains visible. 7 EMPLOYEE Open INPROCESS complaint → Edit → try s_status = CLOSED → Save. V005 error: 'Employees cannot close a complaint'. 8 MANAGER Open INPROCESS complaint → Edit → s_status = CLOSED → closed_on = today → Save. Status badge changes to CLOSED (grey). Edit button disappears (COMPLETED Vienable). actual_tat computed in Data Browser. 9 ALL ROLES Navigate to Home (🏠). Two tiles visible: Dashboard and Complaints. Each tile navigates correctly. 10 ALL ROLES Preview In → Phone (Page Builder). Grid in s_complaints shows only 3 columns (ticket_id, priority, s_status) on phone view.

documents.t: Welcome to the Procify Developer Training. This section explains the overall structure of the course, how sessions are designed, and what is expected of you as a trainee. Read this before starting Session 1.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Training Procedure

documents.t: The training spans 8 sessions. Each session introduces a new layer of the platform — starting with setup and ending with publishing a fully working application. Sessions must be taken in order; each one builds directly on the previous. Session Topic Session 1 Platform Setup & Account Management Session 2 BOL — Entity Fundamentals & Initial Pages Session 3 Entity Configuration (Relations, Object Types, Status, ID Series) Session 4 Value Helps & Queries Session 5 BOL Logic & Validations with dashboard creation Session 6 Bindings, Navigation & Styling Session 7 Controllers & Client-Side Behaviour Session 8 Menu Configuration & App Management, Versioning & Publishing
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Training Procedure

documents.t: This training does not teach concepts in isolation. You will build one real application — a Customer complaint system — across all 8 sessions. Every concept is introduced exactly when you need it to make the next part of that application work. Why this matters for you • You will always know WHY you are doing each step, not just HOW. By Session 8 you will have a working application demonstrating every major platform capability. The application grows session by session — if you miss a step it will affect later sessions. When you encounter a similar situation on a real project, you will have a concrete reference point from training.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Beginner Training Guide/Training Procedure

documents.t: Attend each session with the previous session's assignment completed and verified. Follow steps in this guide during hands-on time — do not skip ahead. Ask questions during the Review & Q&A phase, not during the trainer demonstration. The Application You Will Build • This training guide uses a REAL application: the Customer complaints Application. You are not building a demo — you are building a production-ready application for delivery personnel. Every concept taught in every session is applied directly to build this application. By Session 9 you will have a fully working, published Delivery Agent Application.

documents.t: Developer Level 1 was built as an end-to-end project: one real application the Customer Complaints Application built up session by session. This Level 2 guide follows the same approach: no new application is created. Every session below re-opens the entities, pages, entity files, and controllers already built in Level 1 and extends them with an advanced capability, so trainees see how real applications evolve rather than practicing features in isolation. Topics are drawn from the Training Topics sheet, filtered to entries tagged “Developer Level 2,” and mapped onto concrete enhancements of the existing app. Tool names use the current naming glossary, with legacy names noted where relevant.

documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Developer Level 2 Training Guide/Session 1 — Advanced BOL & Data Modelling

documents.t: Configure Network Modes so offline-relevant properties sync correctly to field devices. Network Mode Types Mode How it works Best use case Online The app talks to the server for every operation — network connectivity is required. Data is read from and written directly to the transactional database; nothing is cached locally. Standard business apps with reliable connectivity — real-time dashboards, approval workflows, anything where data must always reflect the server's current state. Offline The app stores data locally (web SQL) and syncs with the server whenever connectivity is available. Users can keep working through weak or no network. Field service, warehouse, or mobile scenarios where users regularly lose signal (e.g., technicians on-site, drivers, remote inspections). SAP Online All transactions route through SAP via the gateway server; data is read from and written to the SAP server itself, not a local Klobase DB. Apps acting as a front-end to SAP where SAP must remain the system of record for every transaction. SAP Preferred Online Transactions pass through SAP but land in the local web SQL rather than being held only in SAP. Hybrid cases where you want SAP validation/processing but still want a local cache for offline reads or faster access.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Developer Level 2 Training Guide/Session 1 — Advanced BOL & Data Modelling

documents.t: Apply Sort Order and an Entity Index to d_complaints for performance and predictable ordering. Extend the existing Entity Rules with a new auto-escalation rule. Extend the existing Query Rules with role-based field masking. Build a BOL Transaction that commits two entities atomically. A. Get a transaction object — either the one already active in your controller context, or create a fresh one: let txn = await this.createTransaction(); // or use existing this.txn B. Create the first entity using createEntityP(entityName, entityJson?, deepClone?, mappingRule?). This adds the object to the transaction as a "dirty" (uncommitted) object — it isn't written to the database yet: let ent_1 = await txn.createEntityP("d_no_hdr", { short_text: "Header entity", description: "First entity in the transaction" }); C. Create the second entity on the same transaction instance (txn), not a new one — this is what makes both creates part of a single atomic commit: let ent_2 = await txn.createEntityP("d_no_work_order", { short_description: "Related entity", description: "Second entity in the transaction" }); D. (Optional) Lock entities if you need to prevent concurrent edits during the transaction: await txn.trylock('d_no_hdr', 1000); E. Commit both entities together with a single commitP() call. Since both ent_1 and ent_2 are dirty objects on the same txn, one commit persists both to the database as a single unit: await txn.commitP(); What This Session Builds On Developer Level 1 (Sessions 1–5) built d_complaints with its properties, one Entity Rule (onCreateComplaint) and one Query Rule (beforeQ) on q_complaints. This session does not start a new entity — it goes back into the same d_complaints and q_complaints files and adds the advanced BOL capabilities on top.

documents.t: In offline mode the app stores data locally and syncs the local cache and server data whenever it finds connectivity. Browsers and installed mobile apps both support it. Values are read from and written to web SQL.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Developer Level 2 Training Guide/Session 1 — Advanced BOL & Data Modelling

documents.t: Create the app as Offline. In Procify Workspace Hub → App Management, create the app and set the Network Mode. The default is ONLINE. Choose Device, Browser or Both under App/Portal Support. Set entity App Mode. In Procify Data Studio, open the entity's Detail tab and set App Mode to Offline. Set Persists On (Null, Both, Client Only or Server Only) on each entity. With Null, an offline flavor creates the entity in both the server and client DB, and an online flavor only on the server. Create the queries that will sync. Use a Saved Query or Modelled Query. Both can drive Initial Sync. In beforeQuery, call setLoadAll(true). The training guide lists offline apps and Initial Sync as use cases, because all data must load during registration. Configure Initial Sync (Platform Settings → First-Run Sync). Initial sync queries run during registration, and the results are stored in the local (browser) cache. Add archive rules (Platform Settings → Data Sync Settings) so old data doesn't pile up on the device. Select the flavor, click Add, choose the entity or query, then add params (key, operator, value) and save. Rules are stored in m_archive. Value rules: IS_NULL and IS_NOT_NULL take no value, IN and NOT_IN need an array, and LIKE uses %value%. If you archive by query, the properties you add must also appear in the query's WHERE clause, or archiving won't work. Build and publish. The Local Archive guide says to create the saved query, then Initial Sync, then the archive rule, and then build.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Developer Level 2 Training Guide/Session 1 — Advanced BOL & Data Modelling

documents.t: Do a fresh registration on the device or browser. Initial sync runs and populates the local store. The app then runs against local data, and changes sync with the server when connectivity returns. Open the screen that has an archive rule and wait about 3 minutes. Archiving runs in the background when the app opens. Not every app needs the same connectivity behavior. Configure Network Mode at the app level so field teams can keep working when connectivity drops. # Action Detail 1 Set the app network mode In Procify Workspace Hub → App Management, create the app and set the Network Mode. The default is ONLINE. 2 Choose where the app runs Choose where the app runs 3 Set the entity network mode In Procify Data Studio, open the entity's Detail tab and set App Mode to Offline. 4 Set Persists On Choose Null, Both, Client Only or Server Only. With Null, an offline flavor creates the entity in both the server and client DB. 5 Create the sync queries Use a Saved Query or Modelled Query. In beforeQuery, call setLoadAll(true) so all the data loads during registration. 6 Configure First-Run Sync In Platform Settings → First-Run Sync, add the queries that should run during registration. The results are stored in the local cache. 7 Add archive rules In Platform Settings → Data Sync Settings, select the flavor, click Add and choose the entity or query. Then add params (key, operator, value) and save. If you archive by query, the properties must also appear in its WHERE clause. 8 Build and publish Create the saved query, then the initial sync, then the archive rule, and then build. 9 Register a fresh device or browser Initial sync runs and populates the local store (web SQL). 10 Use the app offline The app reads and writes local data. Changes sync with the server when connectivity returns. 11 Check archiving Open the screen that has an archive rule and wait about 3 minutes. Archiving runs in the background when the app opens.

documents.t: onArrive is a property of a TransNode/model path that controls what data (if any) gets set when the parent's data arrives — and whether that propagates to the folded (child) path. Implementation Steps​ Create or select the model path — in Procify Page Builder, click Add on the model tree toolbar (or select an existing transnode) and choose its path name, node type (Entity, Entity Set, Query, or Other), and the entity/query ID. Open the transnode's detail section and locate the onArrive field alongside the other model path properties (folded_from, node_type, set_active_if, etc.). Choose the onArrive value based on the behavior you need: Blank — data is set to the path itself, but not propagated to its folded (child) path. First — the 0th index of the parent entityset is automatically set active for this transnode. History — the previously active index (per unique key) is restored as active when the user returns to this path; this only applies to entityset-type transnodes. None — no data is set on this transnode or its folded child at all. Pair it with set_active_if navigation validation matters. If set_active_if is set to Valid (the default), the framework checks for dirty/invalid objects on navigation and — if onArrive conditions are met — calls the onValidate hook in the entity's <entity_name>.ts file to enforce validation before allowing the transition. Verify parent-child propagation behavior, since onArrive also governs how data cascades between transnode types: Entity/Entityset parent → Query child: the query tied to that entity/entityset is set. Query parent → Entityset child: the query's held entityset is set. Query parent → Entity child: the 0th index of the query's entityset is set. Entityset parent → Entity child: the passed index is set, or — if no index is passed — the index is resolved based on the onArrive value (First/History/None/Blank). Test navigation flows (forward and backward) to confirm the right index/data is restored — this is especially relevant for History, which is the mode that makes list→detail navigation "remember" the last selected row. Make the detail screen smarter about what loads automatically and where links resolve to. # Action Detail 1 Configure onArrive On the detail TransNode, set onArrive to auto-load the 5 most recent related voices — no extra click required. For more details about the OnArrive , see the OnArrive documentation 2 Configure navigateId On the ticket_id link control, set navigateId so it always resolves to pa_complaint_details, whether clicked from p_complaints or the dashboard's embedded timeline. 3 Test both entry points Click a complaint from the main list, then from the dashboard timeline — confirm both land on the same detail area correctly populated.
documents.s: Configuring onArrive on a TransNode (Model Path)
