documents.t: This is managed at runtime via the Role Permissions screen (formerly "Role Permissions") under the Security & Permissions menu (formerly Security & Permissions) — separate from the DEV-time Permission Designer (formerly the Permissions screen in App Builder/App Builder). How runtime assignment works​ Permission groups configured in DEV get pushed to QA/PROD on transport. Once there, they're read-only for structure — permissions can't be added/removed from a DEV-sourced (SYSTEM) group, only enabled/disabled. Admins in QA/PROD can create new groups (marked USER source) and freely add permissions to those. On rollout, existing users get permission groups auto-assigned based on their application role; new users get them assigned at first registration. Versioning behavior: on a major version transport, the newer version's permission groups/permissions overwrite runtime config, and users on the new version get permissions re-adjusted based on role. On a minor version deployment, users still on older versions are not auto-adjusted — permission changes only apply when something version/role/assignment-relevant changes for that user. Implementation steps​ Navigate: Security & Permissions menu → Role Permissions. Advanced Search (mandatory): select an App (required field) — you'll only see groups for apps where you're assigned as Manager. Optionally filter by Enabled and Source (SYSTEM vs USER). Create a group: Click Create, enter a name (uppercase/lowercase/_/-/numbers/spaces, ≤28 characters), then Save to open its detail screen. Assign roles: Go to the Roles tab → Add → pick an application role → Add. Any user holding that role inherits this group's permissions at runtime. Assign custom permissions: Go to the Custom Permissions tab → Add → select the permissions to include → Add. Assign entity (CRUD) permissions: Go to the Entity Permissions section → search for the entity → check the CRUD permissions to grant → confirm. Save the group from the detail header to commit roles + permissions together. Enable/disable as needed: toggle the group's Enabled flag to turn its effect on/off without deleting it (this is the only lever available for SYSTEM-sourced groups). Debugging runtime assignment​ Check what a specific user actually has via the User Access Summary screen (formerly User Access Summary) under Security & Permissions (requires Procify Workspace Hub — formerly Procify Workspace Hub — assigned). Offline/on-device, run: res = await testdb("select r_flavor, r_permission_id from madm_user_permissions") console.log(res[0].rows.map(a => "Flavor : " + a[0] + " . Permission ID : " + a[1]).join("/n")) Simulate an incident requiring temporary elevated access, then audit it. # Action Detail 1 Grant temporary access Create a runtime Role Permission override allowing IT_TEAM_LEAD to Delete during an incident. 2 Use and revoke Apply, test the elevated Delete, then revoke the override. 3 Audit in Permission Logs Confirm both the grant and the revoke appear in Permission Logs with timestamp and actor. ✔ Session 3 Checkpoint ✔ CRUD restrictions enforced server-side for all 3 roles. ✔ IT Team row-level filtering confirmed, including via direct URL access. ✔ Data Access Rule created, assigned, and confirmed via User Access Summary. ✔ Temporary Role Permission granted, used, revoked, and fully audited in Permission Logs.

documents.t: Enable offline access to assigned complaints for field IT Team users via Local Archive. Reduce first-login sync payload using Initial Downloads. Push closed complaints to an external SAP system via Middleware. Bulk-import customer master data using KloSectionXlsx. What This Session Builds On The application has only worked online through Sessions 1–3. This session makes it usable by IT Team members working onsite without connectivity, and adds a bulk-data path for customer onboarding. Scenario An IT Team technician visiting a customer site with no signal can't pull up the complaint they're there to resolve. Every login re-downloads the full complaint history instead of just what's assigned, closed complaints aren't reaching the SAP billing system automatically, and onboarding 20 new customers means entering each one by hand.

documents.t: What it is: Local Archive lets you remove data from a client application's local data store (the on-device/browser database, i.e. web SQL) based on defined criteria. It does not touch the server-side database. Use case: Primarily for offline applications. Since offline mode caches data locally so users can keep working without connectivity, that local store can accumulate old, stale, or unused records over time (completed transactions, historical notifications, etc.). Local Archive lets developers define rules so this data is automatically cleaned from the device/browser in the background — preventing unbounded local storage growth and keeping the offline app performant.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Developer Level 2 Training Guide/Session 4 — Offline, Middleware & Bulk Data

documents.t: Understanding of query parameters (where-clause style conditions). Understanding of Initial Sync and Saved Query concepts — you typically need a saved query and an initial sync set up before the archive rule will behave as expected, since the archive can piggyback on a query's WHERE clause.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Developer Level 2 Training Guide/Session 4 — Offline, Middleware & Bulk Data

documents.t: Local Archive isn't a flag you flip — it activates automatically as soon as an archive rule exists for an entity/query. Once created, the rule is checked in the background whenever the app opens.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Developer Level 2 Training Guide/Session 4 — Offline, Middleware & Bulk Data

documents.t: 1. Navigate to the screen​ Go to Application Settings (formerly Platform Settings) menu header → Data Sync Settings. 2. Select the flavor​ Choose the flavor you're configuring the archive rule for from the dropdown. 3. Add an archive entry​ Click Add. A new line item is created in the m_archive entity with an auto-filled Archive ID (editable if you want a custom value). 4. Select the entity or query​ Click the value help in the Entity/Query Name column and pick the target. If you pick a Query (modeled query), its SQL WHERE clause is also factored into what gets archived. ⚠️ If you pick a query and then add property filters via the Local Archive tool that aren't part of that query's WHERE clause, archiving will silently fail to apply those filters — the query's own WHERE logic takes precedence. 5. Select properties / define filter parameters​ Click the value help icon in the Properties column to open the parameter dialog, then click Add to create a parameter row: Key — the property (from the selected entity/query) to filter on. Operator — the comparison operator. Special cases: IS_NULL / IS_NOT_NULL — no value needed; automatically set to true. IN / NOT_IN — value must be an array, e.g. ["abc","pqr",9]. LIKE — value must be wrapped as %value%. Value — the comparison value (not needed for null checks). If you leave properties unselected entirely, all data for the chosen entity will be deleted rather than a filtered subset. 6. Add the parameter​ Click the Add footer button to attach the parameter to the archive rule. 7. Save​ Click the Save icon to commit the new rule into m_archive. 8. Trigger and verify​ After saving, do a fresh registration and navigate to the screen tied to the archived entity. Wait about 3 minutes — the archive job fires on app open, and matching records are deleted from the local store in the background. # Action Detail 1 Configure archive scope Local Archive on d_complaints and d_complaint_voices for the IT_TEAM role — retain the last 30 days of assigned complaints on-device. 2 Test offline On a device/emulator, disconnect network and confirm assigned complaints and their voice history are still viewable.

documents.t: KloSectionXlsx is a UI control (extends sap.ui.core.Control) that lets developers configure Excel upload and download behavior for a grid/cardlist section — controlling things like the downloaded file's name, a downloadable template, and which columns participate in upload/download. It works hand-in-hand with the Download Excel and Upload buttons exposed by KloSectionToolbar (showDownloadExcel, showUpload properties) — those buttons trigger the behavior; KloSectionXlsx is where you configure how that behavior works. Properties :​ Property Type Default Description fileName string DataDownload Name of the downloaded Excel file. templateFileName string — Name of the template file to be downloaded (used for guided uploads). downloadSectionTemplate string — Section name the download template applies to. uploadSectionTemplate string — Section name the upload template applies to. allColumnsUpload boolean (documented as string) false If true, all entity columns are considered during upload — not just visible ones. allColumnsDownload boolean (documented as string) false If true, all entity columns are included in the downloaded file — not just visible ones.
documents.s: Part D — KloSectionXlsx — Bulk Customer Import
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Developer Level 2 Training Guide/Session 4 — Offline, Middleware & Bulk Data

documents.t: In Procify Page Builder (Procify Page Builder), open the context menu on the grid/cardlist section and Add the Excel Config — this attaches a KloSectionXlsx instance to that section. Set fileName to control the downloaded file's name. If you want users to download a pre-built template rather than an auto-generated one: Place the actual .xlsx file at kloTouch/resources/ExcelTemplates (you'll need to hand this file to the infra team — they place it in that path; it's not something you upload from the UI directly). Set templateFileName to point to it. If no template is found at that path, the system falls back to auto-generating a template based on the columns currently visible on screen. If the template (or download) should include every column on the entity, not just the visible ones, set allColumnsUpload / allColumnsDownload to true as appropriate. Add Excel-based bulk operations to the customer master entity. # Action Detail 1 Add to d_customers Attach KloSectionXlsx to the customer section, enabling bulk Excel upload/download. 2 Bulk import Prepare a sample sheet of 20 customers and import via the section. 3 Verify Confirm all 20 records land correctly in Data Browser. ✔ Session 4 Checkpoint ✔ IT Team can view assigned complaints and voice history fully offline. ✔ Initial download payload measurably reduced and verified. ✔ One closed complaint confirmed pushed to the SAP middleware queue. ✔ 20 customers successfully bulk-imported via KloSectionXlsx.

documents.t: Route escalated complaints through a Manager approval Workflow. Add a nightly Scheduled Task as a server-side safety net for SLA breaches. Notify the right people by Email, SMS, and In-App at the right moments. Deep-link notification emails directly into the relevant complaint. What This Session Builds On Session 1 added a server-side is_escalated flag. This session adds the human workflow and communication layer that reacts to it. Scenario A complaint sits open for a week past SLA with no one following up, because there's no approval step and no nightly check catching it. A customer is never told their complaint was resolved unless someone remembers to call, and a support email can't deep-link straight to the complaint it's about.

documents.t: Diagnose a simulated scheduler failure end-to-end using platform monitoring tools. Confirm notification delivery and resolve a stuck offline sync record. Confirm the SAP middleware payload was processed via Legacy Queue Monitoring. Trace a native control rendering issue on a built APK. Independently verify dashboard numbers using Query Console. What This Session Builds On The app is feature-complete after Sessions 1–6 (automation, offline sync, integrations, reporting). This session is entirely about operating and troubleshooting what was built, not adding new features. Scenario The nightly SLA sweep silently failed last night and nobody noticed until complaints started piling up unflagged. A customer insists they never got a resolution notification, and there's no way to check; finance says a closed complaint never showed up in SAP and nobody can tell whether it's stuck or lost.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Developer Level 2 Training Guide/Session 7 — Monitoring & Troubleshooting

documents.t: Break the Session 5 scheduler on purpose, then find and fix it. # Action Detail 1 Simulate a failure Introduce a bad condition into the nightly SLA-sweep task and trigger it. 2 Observe the failure Confirm the failure appears in Scheduler Monitoring and Task History. 3 Trace the root cause Find the underlying error in Google Logs. 4 Fix and re-run Correct the task and confirm success via Running Tasks. For more details about the scheduler, see the Scheduler documentation.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Developer Level 2 Training Guide/Session 7 — Monitoring & Troubleshooting

documents.t: Confirm the Session 4 and 5 integrations are actually working end-to-end. # Action Detail 1 Verify notifications Check Notification History for the assignment/resolution messages from Session 5 — confirm delivered status. 2 Diagnose a stuck sync Simulate a stuck offline record on Server Queue / Mobile Sync Queue for an IT Team device from Session 4, and resolve it. 3 Check the SAP channel Review Legacy Queue Monitoring to confirm the Session 4 closed-complaint payload to SAP was processed.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Training Guide/Developer Level 2 Training Guide/Session 7 — Monitoring & Troubleshooting

documents.t: Trace a native rendering issue and cross-verify reporting data. # Action Detail 1 Build and test the APK Build a debug APK including the kloRating control from Session 2. 2 Debug if needed If the control fails to render natively, use APK/IPA debugging tools to trace the issue. 3 Cross-verify dashboard data Use Query Console to independently confirm the raw row counts behind the Session 6 dashboard charts. For more details about the Query console, see the Query console documentation. ✔ Session 7 Checkpoint ✔ Simulated scheduler failure diagnosed via Scheduler Monitoring + Google Logs and resolved. ✔ Notification delivery confirmed; one stuck sync record identified and resolved. ✔ SAP payload confirmed processed in Legacy Queue Monitoring. ✔ APK rendering issue for kloRating traced (fixed or root-caused). ✔ Dashboard chart numbers cross-verified against raw data via Query Console.

documents.t: Create a client-specific child flavor using App Inheritance. Apply Customer Branding to the login page, menus, and headers. Version-control all Level 2 code in a Git repo. Migrate the fully enhanced application to QA and confirm every enhancement survived. What This Session Builds On The base Customer Complaints app is now feature-rich after Sessions 1–7. This final session prepares it for a real client rollout — a branded, inherited child flavor, migrated to QA. Scenario The business is onboarding a new client, Acme, who needs their own complaint categories and branded login screen without touching the shared base app every other client depends on. Before go-live, someone has to confirm a departed developer's session is revoked and that the whole app still works correctly once it's moved to QA.
